_comment: Hand-written assessments for the site's Audit section. The numbers beside them are computed by scripts/audit_corpus.py; these are the judgments about what the numbers mean, including where the evidence does not support a judgment. Confidence is about THIS assessment, not about the corpus.

completeness.verdict: Probably complete for catalog-shaped content; unmeasured for everything else.
completeness.basis: 421 of 495 compendium entries from this book resolve to a corpus rule. Most of the 74 that do not are gear whose rules the corpus states as a stat line rather than prose, plus 6 personal effects known to be absent and deferred by decision. But the compendium only enumerates catalog items — techniques, advantages, schools, titles, gear. It says nothing about whether the systems chapters, tables and procedures are whole, and nothing has yet checked the book page by page for content no entity claims.

correctness.verdict: The best in the corpus by a wide margin. Three confirmed defects found and fixed; one open question about content that does not belong here.
correctness.confidence: Moderate to high, and better supported than before
correctness.basis: 607 of 686 judgeable rules strings are printed in the book verbatim (88%). Fixed in this pass, each checked against the page first: the adversity filed as 'Blackmailed by [Name]' now reads 'Blackmailed by [Character's Name]' as the book prints it, which matters because a separate advantage 'Blackmail on [Name]' also exists; the Shadowlands Taint (Earth) adversity said a dead character's body 'rises as an undead creature' where the book names it — 'rises as a Zombie Peasant (see page 321)'; and the four Void-point uses of advantages had been compressed to telegraphic notes ('Convert own advantage to disadvantage if creates logical vulnerability') and are now the book's own sentences. Question 14's invented Demeanor effect was found and fixed on 2026-08-30, with ten drifted question titles and an invented Part structure. One defect remains open: 'Inversion' sits in core-techniques although its own comment says inversions are not in the Core Rulebook — where it should go is a call for you, not for me. Separately, a sample of the strings this method cannot judge was checked against the page images directly. Two complete school entries — Kaiu Engineer and Kitsuki Investigator — verify field for field: rings, the choose-five skill lists, honor, techniques available, starting techniques, starting outfit, all six curriculum ranks, and both abilities word for word, including the symbol notation. A third check on the Unspecified Deadliness list was also verbatim. On that sample the corpus's (op)/(su)/(st)/(ring) tokens are a faithful and consistent transcription of the printed glyphs, which is meaningful evidence that the 238 unjudgeable strings are not hiding a second population of errors. It is still a sample of three passages, not a measurement. A third instrument was added after the two substantive errors found so far both turned out to be invented mechanics rather than dropped text: audit_rules.py reads the RULES labels, which nothing had ever checked, and reports any whose distinctive wording its own entity never uses. Of 1,127 labels corpus-wide it flags 14, seven of them in core. Most are false positives — each_applies_once_per_check is exactly what the book says, and q6_sets_ninjo trips only on a macron — but the check is a lead generator, not a detector, and it is worth being clear about its limit: it would not have caught Shattering Parry, because there the label and the invented text agreed with each other. What catches that class is comparing the entity's text to the page. Widening the string extractor was what exposed both of the last two. It had been reading only standalone quoted lines and prose properties, and was blind to two shapes the corpus states rules in: an indexed entry in an ordered block (DIFFICULTY_SCALE's `2 "An average task…"`) and a named pair (USES's `^"Shattering Parry" "…"`, TENETS's `^"Courtesy (Rei)" "…"`). The Void point rules, the target-number scale and the tenets were all invisible to this audit until those two forms were added — 94 more strings in the core files alone. Every substantive error found so far has come from a place the instrument was not yet looking, which is the honest reason to keep the unjudgeable figure in view.

core.next: The 238 unjudgeable strings need the page images. A page-residue pass would settle the completeness question the compendium cannot. 'Inversion' needs a home.
fixed: Shadowlands Taint (Earth): 'an undead creature' -> 'a Zombie Peasant (see page 321)' (core-adversities 0.4.1)

The four Void-point uses of advantages restored to the book's wording, and the rule for when advantages may be turned — during Step 4, with the GM as final arbiter — added; it was absent entirely (core-character 0.4.3)

The Void Points block in core-base stated the wrong rule for Shattering Parry: 'Reduce severity of a critical strike targeting you by your school rank'. The book says a character spends the point to intercept the attack with their weapon, potentially sacrificing it — reducing severity by school rank is the Crab school ability, not this. The corpus's own gm-screen-reference file described it correctly, so the corpus contradicted itself. All three Void point uses and all four ways of gaining one are now the book's text (core-base 0.4.1).
The same block invented a limit: it capped Void points gained from an adversity at once per scene. The book applies 'Once per scene' to anxieties only. Removed.

'Technique Activation' renamed to the book's heading, 'Techniques and Other Abilities'. The rule hash named shattering_parry_reduction described a mechanic that does not exist and was replaced rather than relabelled.

The target-number difficulty scale was shifted one step across TN 1-6. The corpus called TN 2 'Easy' where the book's easy task is TN 1, and TN 4 'Hard' where the book's difficult task is TN 3, so a GM reading the corpus set every ordinary task one step too high — in the most basic mechanic in the game. All eight entries now carry the book's own descriptions and its worked examples, which had been dropped entirely (core-base 0.4.2).

The seven tenets of Bushidō were wrong in core-character. Three were named for the wrong virtue — the book's Courtesy, Sincerity and Duty and Loyalty were filed as Respect, Honesty and Duty, and the book explicitly says 'Sincerity is more complex than mere Honesty', which is exactly the distinction the old name collapsed. Two more were misspelled (Meyo for Meiyo, Chugo for Chūgi) and Courage had lost its macron. Worse, each carried a 'Championed by the <clan>' attribution — Courage to the Crane, Righteousness to the Crab — and that phrase appears nowhere in the Core Rulebook. Seven invented claims. All seven tenets now carry the book's names and their printed opening lines (core-character 0.4.4). The corpus had been contradicting itself: its own Paragon and Disdain advantages use the correct names. The Creator was unaffected — it reads CLAN_PARAMOUNT_TENETS, a different and correct block.
flagged: 'Inversion' sits in core-techniques as a category placeholder, and its own comment says inversions are not in the Core Rulebook — they appear in Celestial Realms and other supplements. Moving it, or deleting it, is a scope call. Logged, not touched.
'Iaijutsu Duel (to first blood)' is a name the converter coined; the book discusses duelling to first blood but prints no such heading. Harmless, but it is not a book name.

The corpus keeps page cross-references in 35 places and drops them elsewhere. There is no stated convention. Worth settling, because dropped cross-references are the single largest category of drift across the whole corpus.

The Repeated Injury sidebar (Core Rulebook p. 270) is absent from the corpus entirely — a character who would take a second scar disadvantage from recurring harm instead suffers Dying (5 rounds). Found by reading the page image; no text-based check could see it. Not added, because which entity should host a sidebar rule is a structural choice for you.

'Seize the Moment' had lost its timing — the book places the spend in Step 3 and the extra kept die in Step 5. Restored, but it is worth knowing that timing detail is the kind of thing the compression drops most often.

A rule labelled default_tn_is_two sits on Target Number. The book states no default TN — the Sample TNs passage says the GM chooses the number from the difficulty of the task, which this arguably contradicts. Not removed: absence from the extracted text is not proof of absence from the book, and deleting a rule is your call.

completeness.verdict: Meaningful gap against the compendium — 48 entries carry no corpus rule.
completeness.basis: 143 of 191 compendium entries resolve (75%), the second-worst ratio of any book with a corpus file. Worth noting that this book supplies the Creator's alternate twenty-questions path, so gaps here surface in play.

correctness.verdict: Pervasively reworded. Sampled cases preserve meaning but almost none are the book's sentence.
correctness.basis: Only 67 of 255 judgeable strings are verbatim (26%), and 124 of the 188 drifting strings share no long run with the book at all. Hand-checked examples: the corpus writes 'does not need to be purchased. You may immediately perform that ritual' where the book prints 'this does not need to be a ritual you have purchased. You are immediately able to perform that ritual'. Meaning survives; the wording is the converter's. Two item names carry corpus-added glosses — 'Lute (Biwa)' and 'Chandu (Smoking Opium)' where the book prints 'biwa' and 'Chandu'.

path-of-waves.next: Highest-value target after Core: worst verbatim rate, a real completeness gap, and it feeds the Creator.
flagged: 'Lute (Biwa)' and 'Chandu (Smoking Opium)' carry glosses the book does not print — it says 'biwa' and 'Chandu'. Deliberately left alone: the compendium calls the first 'Lute', so renaming the corpus to the book's word would break rules-text resolution. The gloss is doing real work as a bridge between the two vocabularies.

completeness.basis: 67 of 67 compendium entries resolve. The compendium's list for this book is small, so this is weaker evidence than the ratio suggests.

correctness.verdict: Heavily reworded, and the least judgeable book in the corpus.
correctness.basis: 29 of 98 judgeable strings verbatim (30%), but 39% of all strings carry symbol notation and cannot be judged from text at all — the highest proportion anywhere. Sampled drift is a mix of corpus-authored connective text ('Always uses Focus as base initiative value') and compression of the book's sentence.

writ-of-the-wilds.next: Do not draw conclusions here without the page images; nearly two fifths of the content is invisible to this method.

completeness.basis: 64 of 64 compendium entries resolve. This book is largely setting material, which the compendium does not enumerate, so the ratio speaks only for its mechanical items.

correctness.verdict: Substantially reworded; a third of drifting strings share no run with the book.
correctness.basis: 53 of 119 judgeable strings verbatim (45%). Sampled drift includes outfit list fragments where the book interleaves a page cross-reference the corpus drops ('an attendant or Rokugani pony' against 'an attendant (see page 64 of the core rulebook) or Rokugani pony'), and school abilities rewritten in the corpus's own register.

emerald-empire.next: Sample twenty strings against the page before deciding whether this is cosmetic or substantive.

completeness.verdict: Complete against the compendium bar one entry.

correctness.verdict: About half the judgeable text is the book's; the rest is close paraphrase.
correctness.basis: 80 of 166 judgeable strings verbatim (48%). Hand-checked drift tracks the book's own sentence and diverges on small words — the corpus writes 'the identified relationship' where the book prints 'the relationship identified by the ritual'. No substantive error surfaced in the sample, but the sample was three strings.

courts-of-stone.next: Low apparent risk, but the sample is too small to stand on.

correctness.verdict: Reworded throughout; no substantive error confirmed.
correctness.basis: 71 of 186 judgeable strings verbatim (38%). A correction to an earlier version of this page: the Shadowlands Taint defect reported here belongs to the Core Rulebook — the entity lives in core-adversities — and the passage it was compared against was a different rule in this book altogether, matched by accident. Nothing substantive has been confirmed wrong in these two files. Sampled drift is the restructuring seen everywhere else ('Nourish: receive fatigue' for 'If you nourish, you may receive fatigue'), on a sample of three strings.

shadowlands.next: Nothing here is confirmed either way. Sample twenty strings against the page before spending effort on this book.

completeness.verdict: 19 compendium entries carry no corpus rule.

correctness.verdict: The lowest verbatim rate in the corpus, but much of it is corpus-authored annotation rather than misquoted rules.
correctness.basis: 33 of 160 judgeable strings verbatim (21%). 106 of 127 drifting strings share no run with the book. Hand-checked: the komainu entries carry lines the corpus wrote itself ('Modified Manifest Earth Kami (core rulebook p.323)'), and a rewrite of the book's 'the komainu is, in all respects, a large stone statue'. The book text extracts cleanly, so this is the corpus's wording, not extraction damage — I verified that before concluding it.

celestial-realms.next: Decide whether corpus-authored annotation belongs in rules strings at all; it is the bulk of this book's drift.
flagged: Much of this book's drift is annotation the converter wrote itself ('Modified Manifest Earth Kami (core rulebook p.323)') sitting in rules strings rather than in comments. Whether that belongs in rules text at all is a convention question, not a defect to fix string by string.

correctness.verdict: Largely corpus-authored summary lines standing in for the book's procedures.
correctness.basis: 77 of 253 judgeable strings verbatim (30%). Sampled drift is short declarative labels the corpus wrote — 'Accumulate momentum to establish a binding agreement between mortal and spirit', 'Drive out a spirit that has possessed a character' — which describe book procedures without quoting them. These are summaries, not errors, but they are also not rules text.

five-winds.next: Confirm the procedures themselves are carried somewhere, not only their summaries.
flagged: The drift here is short declarative labels the converter wrote to stand in for the book's procedures. Before treating these as errors, confirm the procedures themselves are carried somewhere — the labels may be legitimate index entries pointing at content that exists.

correctness.verdict: Second-best verbatim rate; drift is dominated by dropped page cross-references.
correctness.basis: 174 of 264 judgeable strings verbatim (66%). Sampled drift diverges exactly where the book prints '(see page 114)' and the corpus omits it. The 47 names absent from the book are the converter's own table row labels — '4+ Bonus Successes', 'Hostile lands without resupply' for the book's 'If the army is in hostile lands without a path of resupply'. Checked: the content is present, the label is coined. Not missing content.

fields-of-victory.next: Decide the house rule on page cross-references; it would resolve most of this book's drift at a stroke.

completeness.verdict: Cannot be assessed — the compendium enumerates nothing for this book.
completeness.basis: No compendium entries carry this source, so there is no independent list to measure against. The corpus has 19 entities from a 2-file text extraction.

correctness.verdict: Mostly tracking the book, on a very small sample.
correctness.basis: 15 of 27 judgeable strings verbatim (56%), and 7 of the 12 drifting strings share a long run with the book — the highest proportion of near-misses anywhere, meaning the corpus is quoting and trimming rather than rewriting. 27 strings is too few to generalise from.

legacies-of-war.next: Small enough to verify by hand end to end.

completeness.verdict: Half the compendium's entries for this book carry no corpus rule.
completeness.basis: 11 of 21 compendium entries resolve (52%) — proportionally the worst gap of any book with a corpus file, though the absolute number is small.

correctness.verdict: Light compression of the book's sentences.
correctness.basis: 9 of 20 judgeable strings verbatim. Hand-checked: the corpus drops qualifiers — 'you wake up later' for the book's 'you instead wake up later', '(Games [Fire] to wager on a single gambit)' for 'such as a Games (Fire) check to wager the game on a single gambit'. Meaning intact. 20 strings is a very small sample.

mantis-clan.next: The 10 unresolved compendium entries are the concrete thing to chase here.

completeness.verdict: Complete against the compendium's three entries.
completeness.basis: 3 of 3 resolve, which is almost no evidence either way.

correctness.basis: Five rules strings in total, of which four could be judged. There is nothing here to measure.

gm-kit.next: Verify by hand if it matters; it is small enough to read.

completeness.basis: No compendium entries carry this source. The file is 31 reference panels.

correctness.verdict: Not assessable by this method at all.
correctness.basis: The file contains zero rules strings — its content is written as comments, which this audit does not read because comments are authoring notes elsewhere in the corpus. All 31 names are corpus-coined panel titles ('Dice Symbols Reference'), so the name check says nothing either. This file needs a different technique entirely.

gm-screen.next: Decide whether comment-bodied reference panels are acceptable, or should be promoted to properties as the 2026-05-20 audit did for NPC abilities.
flagged: This file's content is written as comments rather than properties, which is why it has zero rules strings and cannot be audited at all. The 2026-05-20 audit promoted 218 comment-as-data ability DEFs across the NPC files for exactly this reason; this file was not part of that sweep. Promoting it would make it auditable, but it is a structural change to a whole file and needs your sign-off.

completeness.basis: No compendium entries carry this source. It is a promotional letter, not a sourcebook; the corpus has 8 entities.

correctness.basis: Four rules strings, three of them unjudgeable. The one judgeable string tracks the book and diverges on an article ('the Bushi' for 'a bushi').

daidoji-shin.next: Small enough to verify by hand.

completeness.basis: No compendium entries carry this source.

correctness.verdict: Now measurable, and mostly tracking its targets.
correctness.basis: This file is now compared against the Core Rulebook as well as the errata document, because an errata file names the Core entities it corrects. That fix took the absent-name count from 9 of 11 to zero. Three rules strings remains too small a sample to judge.

errata-2019.next: Re-run this file against Core plus the errata document together.

completeness.basis: No compendium entries carry this source.

correctness.verdict: Now measurable, and mostly tracking its targets.
correctness.basis: Compared against Core plus the errata document, the absent-name count fell from 24 to 12, and all twelve that remain are names the converter prefixed onto real content — the book prints the playset 'Blood and Consequences' where the corpus files 'Optional Rule Playset: Blood and Consequences'. 14 of 26 judgeable strings verbatim.

errata-2020.next: Errata correctness matters more than the numbers suggest: these files load last and overwrite everything before them. Worth reading end to end by hand.
